claim.why_it_matters: A numbered section heading printed in the PDF is demoted to a plain paragraph in the markdown; its children 6.2.2.2.1-6.2.2.2.4 on page 105 are headings (####) under a parent that is not one.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of PDF page 104 (II-20) prints '6.2.2.2 Object Attributes' as a bold numbered heading, set off on its own line like 6.2.2.1.1-6.2.2.1.4. In page-104.md (line 25) it is a bare paragraph line '6.2.2.2 Object Attributes' with no '#' marker. On page-105.md its children appear as '#### 6.2.2.2.1 Working Storage Records' through '#### 6.2.2.2.4 Other Objects', so the parent is not a heading while its children are. The text is not lost, but the document's heading hierarchy is broken, and that is what a structural missing-heading claim means. The claim quotes both sources correctly.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as stated. Sibling note: on the same page, 6.2.2.1 Object Types and 6.2.2.1.1-6.2.2.1.4 are also plain paragraph lines in the markdown, although the PDF prints them as headings. Each should be checked or filed on its own.
